X-T15-021.title: Persistent semantic signal graph and resumable read/eval/print

environment.language: ISO C17 with exact-width signed32/unsigned32 and signed64 types
environment.dependencies: Original fixed-array domain/session code; explicitly supplied accepted original pd_lex/pd_pratt/pd_evaluate provider. Stdio/Python are host support. No external graph/parser/runtime library.

passages: The short Semantic Model catalog definition and reference to chapter11
Single Pass Builder: textual configuration constructing a runtime Reader
Two Pass Builder: syntax AST, separate Reader construction, alternate XML syntax and independently testable stages
The Read-Eval-Print Loop: read representation, evaluate, print, repeat; evaluator callback

limitations: Bounded original model/languages, not Scheme or a general DSL framework.
Live-session output recovery is not durable exactly-once delivery.
Author execution is separate from delayed learner, external human and physical observations.

rubric.criterion: Implement the persistent signal domain graph with stable IDs, checked transactional updates, dependency/cycle validation and cached-value propagation; explain why it is not an AST.

levels.0: Missing mechanism or false publication/lifetime claim.
levels.1: Selected examples work but a required condition or independent distinction is absent.
levels.2: Implement the persistent signal domain graph with stable IDs, checked transactional updates, dependency/cycle validation and cached-value propagation; explain why it is not an AST. D1-D3 retain exact source/code/finite-check evidence.
levels.3: Unaided D4 changes the stream/output conditions and defends the resulting state and effect trace.

rubric.criterion: Construct the same semantic model through two actual configuration syntaxes and a direct API, then compose the accepted lexer/Pratt/evaluator for transient queries with grouped symbol values and explicit limits.

rubric.criterion: Implement persistent read/eval/print with command-error recovery, commit-before-reply and prefix-owned output retry; execute the required changed chunk/EOF/failed-print reference without duplicating effects.

objective_coverage.scope: This required companion refines semantic separation; it does not independently discharge the prerequisite tokenizer/parser leaves.
